I've been watching the last years of my grandparents lives unfold. I never really knew them well until they were moved to my home state about 2-3 years ago, to be closer to their adult children (which is not what they wanted, but what their adult children wanted), as they were no longer able to live independently. They've been married for over 70 years and we expect that when one dies, the other one will follow soon.

Recently one grandparent (97 yrs old) had a fall, and had to get hip surgery, after which they were moved from a nice big/roomy house to a small assisted living apartment.

I can tell that my grandpa (who has decent capacity over his mind and is fairly cognizant/aware of what's going on in his life - although he does suffer from short term memory now and then) has been depressed over the past years. I think his (reluctantly resigned/accepted) sense of purpose in life is to enjoy time with his wife while they wait to die, and although assisted living means that he can make new friends with fellow old people and find some fun every day (they provide social activities), he is aware that he has very little control over his life now. One thing I've learned from him, that I haven't really thought about much as an adult, is that as you grow old (IF you grow old enough to reach the point of dependency), you lose control over your life - a lot of control, almost to the point where you are like a doll to be shuffled around where ever your family/finances decide to take you.

It makes me wonder, where do other people see themselves if they ever reach the age where they are no longer fully competent and mobile enough to live independently?

What do you think the ideal lifestyle is like for someone in their 90s? What do you think the reality of your 90s (if you grow old enough) will be like?
If you lived to be 90+, where do you see yourself? How/where do you see yourself living, and what would your day-to-day activities look like?
